profile.reading:
Searcy Information Technologies is listed under the City of Searcy, the municipal government of Searcy, Arkansas, at an address near 101 North Elm Street in the city's downtown core. Searcy is the county seat of White County and a city of roughly 23,000 people in the northeastern part of the state, about fifty miles northeast of Little Rock. It is also home to Harding University, a private university that is one of the city's largest employers alongside city and county government itself.

Unlike the commercial and wholesale data centers elsewhere in this registry, a municipal information technology department like this one is not built or marketed to host outside customers. City IT departments in a community this size typically run and maintain the systems that keep local government functioning day to day: utility billing and metering software for water and electric service, police and fire dispatch and records systems, geographic information system mapping for planning and public works, financial and payroll software, and the servers behind the city's public website and email. That kind of infrastructure is usually housed in a server room or data closet inside a municipal building rather than a purpose built data center, and it is sized for the city's own internal workloads rather than for colocation tenants.

No square footage, power capacity, cooling configuration, or construction date for this specific facility has been published by the City of Searcy, and the city does not appear to operate a public facing municipal broadband or colocation service under the Information Technology name. That is expected rather than unusual. Small city governments generally do not publish technical specifications for internal server infrastructure the way commercial operators do, both because the information has no marketing value to a government department and because publicizing detailed specifications of systems tied to public safety and utility operations offers little benefit and a small security downside. The listing here reflects the address and the operator of record rather than a claim about scale, and it should be read as municipal government infrastructure rather than a commercial data center serving outside tenants. Readers looking for more detail on this specific department are best served by contacting the City of Searcy directly.

reading:
The City of Searcy is the municipal government of a city of roughly 23,000 people in White County, Arkansas, about fifty miles northeast of Little Rock and best known as the home of Harding University. It appears in a data centre registry because a single OpenStreetMap building in its downtown carries the tag telecom=data_center, and that tag has never been reviewed.

The building is the city's Information Technology Building on North Elm Street. The city's own Information Technology page places the department at 107 North Elm Street, while the OpenStreetMap object records 101 North Elm Street, a discrepancy of a few doors on the same block that neither source has reconciled. What the city publishes about the facility is genuine but modest. It describes a network operations centre with 24 hour protected access, remote environmental monitoring and paging, redundant cooling systems, an offsite backup connected by fibre, and a natural gas or propane Generac emergency generator. It reports six storage arrays totalling 210 terabytes with fully automated daily backups, fibre connections to every city department building, and a Cisco enterprise IP telephony system carrying more than 150 desktop phones with voicemail and unified messaging. The department is three people, an IT manager, a network administrator and a support technician, and it also runs computer training for city staff in Excel, Word, Outlook and basic computing.

None of that is a data centre in the sense the rest of this registry uses the word. It is the server room and telephone system of a small city government, sized for utility billing, dispatch, mapping, payroll and the city website, and it is not offered to outside tenants. Searcy publishes no floor area, no utility service figure, no standby generator rating in kilowatts and no IT load, and there is no municipal broadband programme extending city network or internet service to residents or businesses.

The provenance of the registry entry is worth stating plainly. The building outline was created in OpenStreetMap on 13 January 2022 in changeset 116088409, whose comment reads "Add buildings and sidewalks to N Elm St and W Center Ave in Searcy, AR" and whose metadata shows the contributor had just completed the editor's built in walkthrough. The data centre tag was applied when the outline was first drawn, and no later version has revisited it. Aggregating a tag like that without review is how a three person municipal IT department ends up counted alongside wholesale campuses, and it is why the facility count here should be read as one building of unstated size rather than as capacity of any kind.
